about: Georgia Power's current list of major transmission projects, with the counties and project type the company gives on its own website, plus new lines and substations that the 2026 regional transmission plan lists for Georgia Power. Voltage is from each project's name. Year is the regional plan's in-service year where the plan lists the project; Georgia Power's list gives no dates. Read by hand on November 23, 2026; check the sources before quoting.

projects.name: Norcross - South Hall
projects.status: Listed as a current project; the list gives no date
projects.check_note: A federal letter confirms the South Hall substation in Hall County; no second source names the line work. Not in the regional plan's public list.

projects.name: Cash Creek - McGrau Ford
projects.status: Listed as a current project; the list gives no date
projects.check_note: WRDW names the McGrau Ford substation, in Cherokee County; no second source describes this line. Not in the regional plan's public list.

projects.name: Tomochichi - Towaliga River
projects.status: Listed as a current project by Georgia Power; the regional plan gives 2027 as the in-service year
projects.check_note: The regional plan lists a new Tomochichi 500/230 kV station and two new 230 kV lines to a new Towaliga River substation.

projects.name: Big Tazewell - Farley
projects.status: Listed as a current project by Georgia Power; the regional plan gives 2029 as the in-service year
projects.check_note: The regional plan lists a new 500 kV line from Farley (Alabama) to Big Tazewell; a county legal notice also names it.

projects.name: Decatur - Scottdale
projects.status: Listed as a current project; the list gives no date
projects.check_note: Atlanta News First reported the plan and that the Decatur part was paused. The regional plan lists only a jumper replacement on this line, in 2035.

projects.name: Ashley Park - Wansley
projects.status: Listed as a current project by Georgia Power; the regional plan gives 2029 as the in-service year
projects.check_note: The regional plan lists a new 35-mile 500 kV line (in service 2029). Fayette News reports 35.8 miles through Coweta, Fayette, Fulton and Heard and completion in 2028.
